author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Poutine
description: Crisp hand-cut fries topped with cheese curds and warm homemade gravy.
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even fries, rinse away excess starch, and dry them thoroughly before frying.
Fry the potatoes in hot neutral oil until tender, drain them, then fry once more until deeply crisp and golden.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in flour, and cook the roux briefly until it smells lightly toasted.
Whisk in the beef and chicken stocks gradually so the gravy stays smooth, then add tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer the gravy gently until it coats a spoon, tasting only at the end because the stock and cheese curds add salt.
Place the hot fries in warm serving bowls and scatter the cheese curds evenly over the fries just before serving.
Pour the hot gravy over the curds so they soften while the fries retain as much crunch as possible.
Serve immediately; poutine is at its best while the gravy is hot and the cheese curds are only partly melted.
commonMistakes: Letting the fries sit before the final fry.
substitutions: Use a vegetarian gravy if preferred.
storage: Store components separately and reheat before assembling.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Nanaimo Bars
description: Classic no-bake Canadian bars with cocoa crumb base, custard filling and chocolate top.
instructions: Cream the base butter with sugar and cocoa, then blend in the beaten egg over gentle heat until the mixture thickens.
Fold the graham crumbs, coconut, optional walnuts and salt through the cocoa mixture until every crumb is coated.
Press the base firmly into a lined square pan, level the surface, and chill it while preparing the custard layer.
Beat the filling butter with milk or cream, custard powder, confectioners' sugar, vanilla and salt until smooth and spreadable.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the cold base, keeping the layer level so the finished bars cut neatly.
Melt the baking chocolate with the remaining butter just until smooth; do not overheat it or the top may seize.
Spread the chocolate quickly over the filling and chill only until the topping is set but not rock-hard.
Cut with a warm dry knife and keep the bars chilled until serving for clean, defined layers.
tips: Score the chocolate before it becomes completely firm.
substitutions: Omit walnuts for a nut-free version.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Butter Tarts
description: Classic Canadian maple butter tarts in crisp pastry shells.
instructions: Roll the pastry dough, cut twelve circles, and gently fit them into a muffin tin without stretching the pastry.
Whisk melted butter, brown sugar, maple syrup and corn syrup until the sugar is evenly moistened.
Beat in the eggs, vinegar and vanilla only until combined so the filling bakes evenly without becoming overly foamy.
Divide the filling among the cold pastry shells, leaving headroom because the custard rises during baking.
Bake at 425°F for five minutes to set the pastry, then reduce the oven to 350°F without removing the pan.
Continue baking for 15 to 20 minutes until the pastry is golden and the centres are set around the edges.
Cool the tarts in the tin until the filling has settled and can be lifted without breaking the pastry.
Serve at room temperature or slightly warm, allowing the maple filling to remain soft and glossy.
tips: Use a rimmed tray under the muffin pan for easy handling.
substitutions: Use your preferred prepared pastry dough.
storage: Store covered at cool room temperature for one day or refrigerate.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Montreal Smoked Meat Sandwich
description: Cured, smoked and steamed Montreal-style brisket for a classic deli sandwich.
ingredients: equal parts cracked black pepper and cracked coriander seed, for rub
rye bread and mustard, to serve
instructions: Trim the brisket as shown, then combine Prague powder #1 with salt and all listed curing spices before rubbing it over the meat.
Cure the brisket under refrigeration, turning it as demonstrated in the video so the seasoning contacts the meat evenly.
Rinse away excess surface cure and dry the brisket thoroughly before applying the equal-parts pepper and coriander rub.
Smoke the brisket at a steady low temperature until the exterior is dark, aromatic and the meat has taken on smoke.
Rest the smoked brisket briefly, then steam it gently until the collagen has softened and the meat slices tenderly.
Slice the finished brisket thinly across the grain while it is hot, preserving moisture in every slice.
Pile the slices generously on rye bread and add mustard immediately before serving as a Montreal-style sandwich.
Keep any remaining meat tightly wrapped and reheat it with steam rather than dry heat to protect its texture.
tips: Use Prague powder #1 only in the measured amount.
commonMistakes: Using curing salt interchangeably with table salt.
substitutions: Do not substitute another curing salt strength.
storage: Refrigerate sliced meat and reheat with steam.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Montreal Bagels
description: Hand-rolled, honey-boiled and seed-coated Montreal-style bagels.
ingredients: sesame seeds, poppy seeds or everything bagel mix
instructions: Stir the warm water, yeast and sugar together and allow the yeast mixture to become foamy before adding it to flour.
Combine bread flour and salt, add the yeast mixture and olive oil, then knead until the dough is smooth and supple.
Cover the dough and let it proof until doubled, then divide it into twelve equal pieces for evenly sized bagels.
Shape each piece into a rope, join and roll the ends together, then rest the formed bagels on a floured surface.
Preheat the oven to 450°F and bring a shallow pot of water with honey to a gentle simmer.
Boil each bagel in the honey water for about 45 seconds per side, then lift it out with a slotted spoon.
Press the wet bagels into the chosen seed topping and arrange them on a lined baking sheet without crowding.
Bake for about 16 minutes until golden, then cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
tips: Keep the honey bath at a gentle simmer.
commonMistakes: Skipping the second short rest after shaping.
substitutions: Choose sesame, poppy or everything topping.
storage: Freeze cooled bagels in an airtight bag.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Peameal Bacon Sandwich
description: A peameal bacon sandwich with tomato, iceberg, melted cheese and bomba mayonnaise.
instructions: Slice the tomatoes and shred the iceberg lettuce so the cold toppings are ready before the bacon begins cooking.
Combine the mayonnaise with three to four tablespoons of bomba sauce and stir until the spread is smooth and evenly coloured.
Butter the cut sides of the kaiser rolls and toast them in a pan until golden, then keep them warm.
Pan-fry the peameal bacon for two to three minutes per side until cooked through and lightly browned at the edges.
Place the cheddar and provolone over four bacon slices so the cheeses begin to melt from the residual heat.
Spread the bomba mayonnaise on the toasted rolls, then arrange tomato and shredded iceberg lettuce on the bases.
Add four bacon slices to each roll, positioning the cheese-topped slices so the filling is evenly distributed.
Close the sandwiches and serve immediately while the rolls are crisp and the peameal bacon is hot.
tips: Use the user-approved video's quantities exactly.
substitutions: Keep the listed cheese blend for video alignment.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Canadian Sausage Breakfast Casserole
description: Hash browns, sausage, vegetables, cheddar and eggs baked into a hearty breakfast casserole.
ingredients: 2 cups diced frozen hash browns (255 grams)
1 red bell pepper, diced (about 1 cup / 120 grams)
instructions: Butter a 13-by-9-inch baking dish and spread the diced frozen hash browns evenly across the bottom of the dish.
Brown the breakfast sausage in a skillet, breaking it into small pieces, then drain excess fat only if necessary.
Cook the onion and red bell pepper in the skillet until softened, add minced garlic, and cook just until fragrant.
Scatter the sausage and cooked vegetables over the hash browns, then distribute the shredded cheddar evenly on top.
Whisk eggs, heavy cream, whole milk, Tabasco, salt, pepper and optional nutmeg together until completely blended.
Pour the egg mixture slowly over the casserole so it settles around the potatoes, sausage, vegetables and cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 40 to 45 minutes until the centre is set and a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Rest the casserole for several minutes before cutting so the egg custard firms and each serving holds together.
tips: Use the newly generated sausage-only image for this renamed recipe.
commonMistakes: Using bacon or ham instead of the video recipe's sausage.
storage: Refrigerate cooled portions for up to three days.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Maple Glazed Salmon
description: Allrecipes maple salmon with a sweet maple-soy garlic glaze.
instructions: Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, minced garlic, garlic salt and black pepper together in a shallow glass baking dish.
Cut the salmon into four equal fillets and coat each piece thoroughly in the maple-soy mixture.
Cover the dish and marinate the salmon in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, turning the fillets once halfway through.
Preheat the oven to 400°F while the salmon finishes marinating, ensuring the oven is fully hot before baking.
Arrange the marinated salmon in the baking dish so the fillets are in a single layer and can cook evenly.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and is cooked through; check early if the fillets are thin.
Spoon some of the warm maple-soy mixture from the dish over each cooked fillet immediately before serving.
Serve the salmon hot, taking care not to overcook it because the sweet glaze can darken quickly in the oven.
tips: Use the priority Allrecipes video and its matching recipe.
substitutions: Use skin-on or skinless salmon fillets.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat gently.

author: Thejan Mahakumbura
title: Maple Chicken
description: Maple syrup chicken breasts with soy, lemon, garlic and ginger.
instructions: Whisk maple syrup, soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, ginger and pepper together in a shallow dish until the marinade is smooth.
Add the chicken breasts, turn to coat, cover the dish, and refrigerate for two hours while turning once.
Coat an indoor grill pan or cast-iron skillet with cooking spray and heat it over medium heat before adding chicken.
Remove the chicken from the marinade while reserving the marinade in a small saucepan for the finishing sauce.
Cook chicken until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reaches 160°F to 165°F, about three to five minutes per side.
Bring the reserved marinade to a simmer over medium heat and cook until it reduces by about half, around four minutes.
Baste the cooked chicken generously with the reduced maple sauce, allowing the glaze to coat the surface evenly.
Rest briefly, slice if desired, and serve immediately with the remaining warm reduced sauce.
tips: Reserve the marinade before it touches cooked chicken.
commonMistakes: Serving the raw marinade without boiling it.
substitutions: Use regular soy sauce as shown by the video creator if needed.
storage: Refrigerate cooled chicken in an airtight container.
